Package neqsim.process.diagnostics

Class OscillationAnalyzer

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.diagnostics.OscillationAnalyzer
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public class OscillationAnalyzer extends Object implements Serializable
Spectral diagnostics for slow periodic oscillations in process time series, such as a pressure cycle of several minutes on a gas node.

The analyser answers the questions that decide how an oscillation must be treated:

  • what is the period and how much of the signal variance sits in the band around it (OscillationAnalyzer.Result.getBandRms());
  • is it a noise-driven, lightly damped mode or a constant-amplitude limit cycle - the coefficient of variation of the amplitude envelope is about 0.52 for a narrow-band Gaussian signal (Rayleigh envelope) and falls towards 0.1 to 0.2 for a limit cycle (OscillationAnalyzer.Result.getEnvelopeCv());
  • how sharp is the peak (OscillationAnalyzer.Result.getQ(), OscillationAnalyzer.Result.getDampingRatioEstimate()) and are there harmonics (OscillationAnalyzer.Result.getSecondHarmonicRatio()) that point to a non-linearity such as a limiter or a burst valve;
  • how does another signal relate to the oscillation - coherence, phase and gain at the peak frequency (crossSpectrum(double[], double[], double)).

Spectra are Welch estimates (Hann window, 50 % overlap, linear detrend per segment). The segment length is a power of two and sets the frequency resolution; a peak whose half-power width is below two bins is flagged as resolution-limited, and its Q is then a lower bound. 

 OscillationAnalyzer a = new OscillationAnalyzer(10.0);
 OscillationAnalyzer.Result r = a.analyze(pressure, 120.0, 1200.0);
 double periodMin = r.getPeakPeriodSeconds() / 60.0;
 OscillationAnalyzer.CrossResult c = a.crossSpectrum(pressure, speed, r.getPeakFrequencyHz());
 double phase = c.getPhaseDegrees(); // positive: speed leads pressure

  • Method Details

    • setSegmentLength

      public void setSegmentLength(int samples)
      Sets the Welch segment length. It is rounded down to a power of two. A longer segment gives finer frequency resolution and a more reliable Q, at the cost of fewer averages.
      Parameters:
      samples - segment length in samples, at least 16; 0 selects an automatic length

    • inflowPhasor

      public double[] inflowPhasor(double[] pressure, double[] massFlowOut, double frequencyHz, double gasVolumeM3, double densityPressureDerivative)
      Gas-node mass-balance phasor at one frequency: the gas inflow implied by the measured compressor flow and the pressure rate of change, per unit of pressure.

      With V the gas volume and rho' = d rho / dP, the balance is F_in = m_out + V rho' dP/dt. At angular frequency w the implied inflow per unit pressure is G_m + j w V rho', where G_m is the complex gain from pressure to the compressor mass flow. The phase of the result tells whether the oscillation sits in the inflow and, for a feedback path with negative gain, the delay of that path.

      Parameters:
      pressure - pressure signal in bar
      massFlowOut - total compressor mass flow out of the node in kg/s
      frequencyHz - frequency of interest in Hz
      gasVolumeM3 - gas volume of the node in m3
      densityPressureDerivative - d rho / dP in kg/m3 per bar (isothermal)
      Returns:
      array of {gain magnitude in kg/s per bar, phase in degrees (positive: inflow leads pressure), implied feedback delay in seconds for a negative-gain feedback path}
